title: The Calculator Won't Dose on Stale Numbers Anymore | vitalii.no
description:
Artem's insulin calculator used whatever IKF, basal insulin and weight values were last saved, even if they were weeks old, even if his weight had drifted far enough that the insulin-to-carb ratio no longer matched his body. The save button was always live, so a stale number could silently produce a wrong dose with no warning at all.

A confirmation gate was added to the calculator. Three value groups — IKF, basal and weight — each carry their own 'valid until' date set from the doctor's history, with a default window of 7 days for IKF and basal and 30 days for weight. The save button now stays disabled until all three are confirmed fresh, and a status card marks each group with a colored indicator. A separate check compares the current weight against the value the doctor's numbers were set for, flagging the drift instead of changing the dose automatically — the parent is asked to check with the doctor.

A dose can no longer be calculated from numbers that are weeks past their confirmation window, and if Artem's weight shifts by more than 5 percent, the calculator now surfaces a warning instead of calculating through it silently.
